request.query: LaunchUnelevated says Access is denied. Administrator preflight passed and using the RunAs popup did not help.

response.headline: Skip another elevation retry: the ordinary worker cannot launch
response.next_step: Use an ordinary coordinator to start the ordinary worker directly, with a separate elevated controller for WPR. For the existing repaired workflow, inspect controller startup confirmation next; do not repeat elevation as a repair for the old LaunchUnelevated failure.
what_matches: The ordinary worker/helper could not launch

failed_attempts.action: Run the old capture wrapper with an administrator controller
failed_attempts.outcome: Administrator preflight passed; worker launch failed with Access denied

failed_attempts.action: Retry the old wrapper through the explicit RunAs popup
failed_attempts.outcome: The same worker-launch stage failed after administrator preflight passed

evidence.title: Skip another elevation retry: the ordinary worker cannot launch
observations: Two recorded elevated capture attempts passed Administrator preflight and failed inside LaunchUnelevated before WPR started.
The generic Access denied message did not identify the exact native API that failed.
The replacement ordinary coordinator launched and owned its ordinary worker directly; the elevated controller owned tracing only.
The replacement worker became ready and remained non-admin. Full live capture still did not complete.
limits: Worker startup was verified; successful physical disk attribution was not.
The exact native call responsible for the old Access denied error remains unidentified.
Only one of the two reported attempts explicitly used RunAs; do not label both as RunAs attempts.

sources.section: Revised disk launch and bounded live outcome
sources.excerpt: Both passed Administrator preflight and failed at unelevated_worker_ready inside LaunchUnelevated, before WPR start. Generic Access denied does not identify the native API that failed; outer PowerShell HRESULT 0x80131501 is not that native error.

sources.section: Explicit RunAs popup result
sources.excerpt: After an explicit RunAs popup, the reported stage remained unelevated_worker_ready and LaunchUnelevated again reported Access is denied.

sources.section: Revised disk launch and bounded live outcome
sources.excerpt: The ordinary worker became ready and remained non-admin.

evidence.title: A System32 prompt does not prove administrator privileges
observations: The historical trace controller recorded controller_windows_administrator=false.
WPR returned Access is denied with 0x80070005; no capture started.
Being in a system directory did not establish elevation.
Later captures passed Administrator preflight and encountered a different worker-launch failure.
limits: Do not apply this recommendation when administrator preflight has already passed.
Elevation alone did not complete the later tracing workflow.

sources.section: Disk diagnostic
sources.excerpt: Its own metadata/status record controller_windows_administrator: false; the profile validated but no capture started. All seven original files still match recorded hashes. Shell location does not establish elevation.

sources.section: Revised disk launch and bounded live outcome
sources.excerpt: Both passed Administrator preflight and failed at unelevated_worker_ready inside LaunchUnelevated, before WPR start.

evidence.title: The worker is ready, but the trace controller never confirms startup
observations: The ordinary worker became ready and remained non-admin.
No controller launch/status, go signal, WPR-start output, or ETL arrived within the 120-second startup window.
The coordinator cancelled the waiting worker and verified owned-worker cleanup.
Zero calibration reads completed; the recording clock never began.
limits: This result does not prove UAC was refused, that a prompt was visible, or that Windows denied privileges.
No successful full capture or device-byte measurement is established.
This submission does not require another trace attempt.

sources.section: Revised disk launch and bounded live outcome
sources.excerpt: No controller launch/status, go signal, WPR-start output or ETL arrived within the separate 120-second startup/UAC window. The coordinator then sent a matching cancellation and verified owned-worker cleanup. Completed calibration reads were zero.

evidence.title: Extraction stopped before loading the model because RAM headroom was low
observations: The first extraction attempt refused available RAM below its 1536 MiB preflight before loading the model.
The second extraction passed after headroom recovered.
The failed preflight produced no model or replay measurements.
limits: The record does not identify a specific application to close or establish a universal RAM requirement.
Do not silently lower the preflight threshold or count the refused attempt as a completed model run.

sources.section: Identities, validation and failure history
sources.excerpt: Its first attempt refused current RAM below the 1,536 MiB preflight before model loading. The second extraction passed after headroom recovered.

evidence.title: Moss is installed, but authenticated queries are blocked
observations: Cycle one found the SDK installed but both required credential variables absent. No genuine query ran.
Cycle two loaded the two variables through the private runtime environment; authentication and eight native validation checks passed.
Only credential presence and authentication status were published.
limits: This remedy addresses missing credentials, not every authentication or connectivity error.
Never paste keys into this demo or commit them to a repository.

sources.section: Genuine Moss: implemented boundary, blocked query
sources.excerpt: Both credential variables were absent. Session opening, native ranking/filter validation, query latency, native index memory, and offline/network measurements remain blocked or null in moss_status.json.

sources.section: Credentials and genuine native validation
sources.excerpt: Both required values were present and authenticated; no values, hashes or lengths were displayed.

A two-order diagnostic reproduced Torch-first failure and Moss-first success.
Bootstrapping genuine Moss before importing Torch repaired the recorded smoke run.
limits: The exact DLL-level cause was not isolated.
The recorded import-order repair is specific evidence from this Windows environment, not a universal fix for error 1114.
